editorial:
Right after the events of the last film, Michael Myers breaks free from Laurie Strode's trap and starts killing again. Laurie is stuck in the hospital recovering from her injuries, but her words push her daughter Karen, granddaughter Allyson, and the whole town of Haddonfield to fight back. You get a bigger, bloodier story this time, with more characters and more chaos. The vibe is tense and angry, like the whole town is ready to explode.

The action is bigger and the body count is high, which horror fans will love. Jamie Lee Curtis is great even from a hospital bed, and the mob scenes feel raw and intense. On the downside, the story jumps around a lot and some characters make silly choices. If you want a tight, smart thriller, this might frustrate you. But if you just want Michael Myers causing mayhem, you will have a blast.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the angry mob corners Michael and beats him down, thinking he is dead. But he gets back up and kills them all one by one. Then he walks to Laurie's house and kills Karen, Laurie's daughter, stabbing her in the back. Laurie is still in the hospital and does not know yet. The movie ends with Michael standing in the house, showing he is still unstoppable and the fight is far from over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slasher horror and Michael Myers.
